localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute hypogastric pain, nausea, and localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen, which are classic symptoms of acute appendicitis.
The abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, along with the abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship, suggest intestinal malrotation.
The elevated white-cell count and rebound tenderness suggest an inflammatory process, which could be indicative of inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient's symptoms of nausea and abdominal discomfort could be indicative of gastroenteritis.
The clustered loops and prominent vessels suggest mesenteric congestion.
The patient's symptoms of right lower quadrant pain and tenderness could be indicative of a right lower quadrant pain syndrome.
The abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, along with the clustered loops, could suggest a small bowel obstruction.
The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and tenderness could be indicative of diverticulitis.

rationales.F01: Acute hypogastric pain is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in various abdominal conditions.
rationales.F06: A positive McBurney’s sign is highly suggestive of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F07: Rebound tenderness is a significant indicator of peritoneal irritation, often seen in acute appendicitis.
rationales.F09: An abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure can be indicative of intestinal malrotation.
rationales.F11: An abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship is a key feature of intestinal malrotation.
rationales.F12: A normal-appearing appendix on imaging makes acute appendicitis less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The abnormally low transverse colon, right colic flexure, and abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship support intestinal malrotation, with no strong contradictions.
